facts.statement: Deinocheirus lived during the Late Cretaceous approximately 70 million years ago.
facts.quote: Deinocheirus ( ) is a genus of large ornithomimosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous around 70 million years ago.

facts.statement: The first remains of Deinocheirus were discovered in 1965 in the Nemegt Formation of Mongolia.
facts.quote: In 1965, a pair of large arms, shoulder girdles, and a few other bones of a new dinosaur were first discovered in the Nemegt Formation of Mongolia.

facts.statement: The genus was formally established with the species Deinocheirus mirificus in 1970.
facts.quote: In 1970, this specimen became the holotype of the only species within the genus, Deinocheirus mirificus

facts.statement: The genus name Deinocheirus translates from Greek to mean "horrible hand".
facts.quote: The genus name is Greek for "horrible hand".

facts.statement: Polish paleontologist Zofia Kielan-Jaworowska discovered the first remains on July 9, 1965.
facts.quote: The first known fossil remains of Deinocheirus were discovered by Polish palaeontologist Zofia Kielan-Jaworowska on July 9, 1965

facts.statement: Halszka Osmólska and Ewa Roniewicz named the holotype specimen in 1970.
facts.quote: The specimen was made the holotype of Deinocheirus mirificus, named by Halszka Osmólska and Ewa Roniewicz in 1970.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was originally cataloged as ZPal MgD-I/6 but is now known as MPC-D 100/18.
facts.quote: The original specimen number of the holotype was ZPal MgD-I/6, but it has since been re-catalogued as MPC-D 100/18.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus was the largest ornithomimosaur, reaching 11 meters in length and weighing 6.5 tons.
facts.quote: Deinocheirus was an unusual ornithomimosaur, the largest of the clade at 11 m long, and weighing 6.5 t.

facts.statement: Tall neural spines on its vertebrae formed a sail along its back.
facts.quote: Its vertebrae had tall neural spines that formed a "sail" along its back.

facts.statement: The skull was 1.024 meters long, featuring a wide bill and deep lower jaw similar to hadrosaurs.
facts.quote: The skull was 1.024 m long, with a wide bill and a deep lower jaw, similar to those of hadrosaurs.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus is thought to have been omnivorous, with evidence including fish scales found near a specimen and gastroliths in its stomach region.
facts.quote: Deinocheirus is thought to have been omnivorous; its skull shape indicates a diet of plants, fish scales were found in association with one specimen and gastroliths were also present in the stomach region of the specimen.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus is classified as a primitive ornithomimosaurian closely related to Garudimimus and Beishanlong, forming the family Deinocheiridae.
facts.quote: After more complete remains were found, Deinocheirus was shown to be a primitive ornithomimosaurian, most closely related to the smaller genera Garudimimus and Beishanlong, together forming the family Deinocheiridae.

facts.statement: Pygostyle-like vertebrae at the end of the tail indicate that Deinocheirus possessed a fan of feathers.
facts.quote: The tail ended in pygostyle-like vertebrae, which indicate the presence of a fan of feathers.

facts.statement: Parts of the 2014 specimens were looted from Mongolia years prior but were repatriated in 2014.
facts.quote: Parts of these new specimens had been looted from Mongolia some years before, but were repatriated in 2014.

facts.statement: Two new Deinocheirus specimens were announced in 2013 at the Society of Vertebrate Paleontology conference.
facts.quote: In 2013, the discovery of two new Deinocheirus specimens were announced before the annual Society of Vertebrate Paleontology (SVP) conference by Lee, Barsbold, Currie, and colleagues.

facts.statement: The two new Deinocheirus specimens were formally described in 2014 by a team including Lee, Barsbold, Currie, Kobayashi, Godefroit, and others.
facts.quote: In 2014, the specimens were described by Lee, Barsbold, Currie, Yoshitsugu Kobayashi, Hang-Jae Lee Lee, Godefroit, Escuillié, and Tsogtbaatar Chinzorig.

facts.statement: Looted Deinocheirus fossils were repatriated to Mongolia on May 1, 2014, following a ceremony at the Mongolian Academy of Sciences.
facts.quote: On May 1, 2014, the fossils were repatriated to Mongolia by a delegation from the Belgian Museum, during a ceremony held at the Mongolian Academy of Sciences.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Thomas R. Holtz described the Deinocheirus skeleton as resembling a hybrid between a hadrosaur and Gallimimus.
facts.quote: American palaeontologist Thomas R. Holtz stated in an interview that the new Deinocheirus remains looked like the "product of a secret love affair between a hadrosaur and Gallimimus".

facts.statement: Deinocheirus is the largest known ornithomimosaur, with the largest specimen estimated to be 11 meters long and weigh 6.36 tons.
facts.quote: Deinocheirus is the largest ornithomimosaurian (ostrich dinosaur) discovered; according to the 2014 description, the largest known specimen measured about 11 m long, with an estimated weight of 6.36 t.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Deinocheirus could reach a length of 11.5 meters and a mass of 5 tons in 2016.
facts.quote: In 2016, Gregory S. Paul presented a higher length estimate of 11.5 m but a lower mass estimate of 5 t.

facts.statement: Thomas R. Holtz estimated the length of Deinocheirus to be 12 meters in 2012.
facts.quote: Holtz estimated the length of Deinocheirus at 12 m in 2012.

facts.statement: A 2020 study by Campione and Evans estimated Deinocheirus body mass at either 6.5 or 7.3 tons depending on the calculation method.
facts.quote: In 2020, Campione and Evans gave a body mass estimate of approximately 6.5 t or 7.3 t depending on calculation method they used.

facts.statement: The only known Deinocheirus skull measures 1.024 meters in length from the premaxilla to the occipital condyle.
facts.quote: The only known skull, belonging to the largest specimen, measures 1.024 m from the premaxilla at the front to the back of the occipital condyle.

facts.statement: The widest part of the Deinocheirus skull behind the eyes is only 23 centimeters wide.
facts.quote: The widest part of the skull behind the eyes is only 23 cm wide in comparison.

facts.statement: The bone walls of the Deinocheirus skull were very thin, measuring about 6 millimeters.
facts.quote: The skull bone walls were rather thin, about 6 mm.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus possessed a rounded, flattened beak that would have been covered by keratin when alive.
facts.quote: It had a rounded, flattened beak, which would have been covered by keratin in life.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus had nostrils turned upwards and a nasal bone shaped like a narrow strap extending above the eye sockets.
facts.quote: The nostrils were turned upwards, and the nasal bone was a narrow strap that extended up above the eye sockets.

facts.statement: The scleral rings in the Deinocheirus eyes had an outer diameter of 8.4 centimeters.
facts.quote: The outer diameter of the scleral rings in the eyes was small, 8.4 cm, compared to the size of the skull.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus had toothless, down-turned jaws where the lower jaw was massive and deep compared to the slender upper jaw.
facts.quote: The jaws were toothless and down-turned, and the lower jaw was very massive and deep compared to the slender and low upper jaw.

facts.statement: The Deinocheirus snout was spatulate and 25 centimeters wide, wider than the skull roof.
facts.quote: The snout was spatulate (flared outwards to the sides) and 25 cm wide, which is wider than the skull roof.

facts.statement: Large three-toed tracks found in the Nemegt locality may have been made by Deinocheirus, as its feet were similar to hadrosaur feet despite the tracks resembling hadrosaur tracks.
facts.quote: Though the tracks were similar to those of hadrosaurs, no tracks of hadrosaur hands were identified, and since the feet of Deinocheirus are now known to have been similar to those of hadrosaurs, it cannot be ruled out that the tracks were made by this genus.

facts.statement: Researchers tested geochemical methods to identify poached Deinocheirus fossils because proving provenance became a scientific and political concern.
facts.quote: Therefore, a study tested the possibility of identifying poached fossils by geochemical methods, using Deinocheirus and other Nemegt dinosaurs as examples.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus and Therizinosaurus have the longest forelimbs of any known bipedal dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Deinocheirus and Therizinosaurus possessed the longest forelimbs known for any bipedal dinosaurs.

facts.statement: The holotype forelimbs of Deinocheirus measure 2.4 meters in total length, including 19.6 cm recurved claws.
facts.quote: The holotype forelimbs measure 2.4 m long – the humerus (upper arm bone) is 93.8 cm, the ulna 68.8 cm, and the hand is 77 cm – including the 19.6 cm recurved claws.

facts.statement: Rough areas and impressions on Deinocheirus forelimbs indicate the presence of powerful muscles.
facts.quote: Various rough areas and impressions on the forelimbs indicate the presence of powerful muscles.

facts.statement: Deep furrows on Deinocheirus arm bone articular surfaces indicate thick pads of cartilage between the joints.
facts.quote: Most articular surfaces of the arm bones were deeply furrowed, indicating that the animal had thick pads of cartilage between the joints.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus had ten low and long neck vertebrae that formed a more S-curved neck than other ornithomimosaurs due to its large skull.
facts.quote: The ten neck vertebrae were low and long, and progressively shorter backwards from the skull. This resulted in a more S-curved neck than seen in other ornithomimosaurs, due to the larger skull.

facts.statement: Most of Deinocheirus vertebrae were highly pneumatized by air sacs connected to the respiratory system, except for the atlas and hindmost tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: All the vertebrae were highly pneumatized by invading air sacs, except for the atlas bone and the hindmost tail-vertebrae, and were thereby connected to the respiratory system.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus possessed a U-shaped wishbone, a feature not found in other ornithomimosaurs.
facts.quote: The wishbone (furcula), an element not known from any other ornithomimosaurs, was U-shaped.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus foot claws were blunt and broad-tipped, resembling those of large ornithischian dinosaurs rather than other theropods.
facts.quote: The claw bones of the feet were blunt and broad-tipped instead of tapered, unlike other theropods, but resembled the unguals of large ornithischian dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Osmólska and Roniewicz created the new family Deinocheiridae within Carnosauria because they believed Deinocheirus did not fit existing theropod families.
facts.quote: Osmólska and Roniewicz initially concluded that Deinocheirus did not belong in any already named theropod family, so they created a new, monotypic family Deinocheiridae, placed in the infraorder Carnosauria.

facts.statement: In 1971, John Ostrom proposed that Deinocheirus belonged to Ornithomimosauria despite having mixed characteristics.
facts.quote: In 1971, John Ostrom first proposed that Deinocheirus belonged with the Ornithomimosauria, while noting that it contained both ornithomimosaurian and non-ornithomimosaurian characters.

facts.statement: In 1976, Rhinchen Barsbold named the order Deinocheirosauria to include Deinocheirus and Therizinosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1976, Rhinchen Barsbold named the order Deinocheirosauria, which was to include the supposedly related genera Deinocheirus and Therizinosaurus.

facts.statement: A 2006 study suggested Deinocheirus was possibly the most primitive ornithomimosaur, but could not confirm this due to missing skull and hindlimb fossils.
facts.quote: A 2006 study by Kobayashi and Barsbold found Deinocheirus to be possibly the most primitive ornithomimosaur, but was unable to further resolve its affinities, due to the lack of skull and hindlimb elements.

facts.statement: Paraxenisaurus from Mexico was named in 2020 as the first known deinocheirid from North America.
facts.quote: In 2020, the deinocheirid Paraxenisaurus from Mexico was named, making it the first member of the group known from North America.

facts.statement: A 2014 cladogram suggested ornithomimosaurians split into Deinocheiridae and Ornithomimidae lineages in the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: The 2014 cladogram suggested that ornithomimosaurians diverged into two major lineages in the Early Cretaceous: Deinocheiridae and Ornithomimidae.

facts.statement: Deinocheirids were not built for running, unlike other ornithomimosaurians.
facts.quote: Unlike other ornithomimosaurians, deinocheirids were not built for running.

facts.statement: Deinocheirids and smaller ornithomimids lacked teeth, unlike more primitive ornithomimosaurs.
facts.quote: Deinocheirids and the smaller ornithomimids did not have teeth, unlike more primitive ornithomimosaurs.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest deinocheirids either originated in Laurasia or dispersed across Northern Hemisphere polar regions, similar to other Asian-affinity dinosaur groups.
facts.quote: Its describers suggested deinocheirids originated in Laurasia (the northern supercontinent of the time) or that they dispersed across polar regions in the Northern Hemisphere, and a similar interchange is also known to have occurred in other dinosaur groups with Asian affinities during the Campanian–Maastrichtian ages.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus likely used its long arms and blunt claws for digging and gathering plants.
facts.quote: The blunt and short hand-claws of Deinocheirus were similar to those of the therizinosaur Alxasaurus, which indicates the long arms and claws were used for digging and gathering plants.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus likely had blunt foot claws to prevent sinking while wading.
facts.quote: The blunt claws of the feet could have helped the animal from sinking into substrate when wading.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus moved slowly due to its robust hind limbs and hip region.
facts.quote: The robust hind limbs and hip region indicates the animal moved slowly.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus's large size may have offered protection from predators like Tarbosaurus but reduced its running speed compared to other ornithomimosaurs.
facts.quote: The large size of the animal may have protected it against predators such as Tarbosaurus, but in turn it lost the running ability of other ornithomimosaurs.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus likely used its long neural spines and possible tail fan for display behaviors.
facts.quote: The long neural spines and possible tail fan may have been used for display behaviour.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus was likely diurnal, as indicated by its relatively small scleral rings compared to skull length.
facts.quote: Deinocheirus was likely diurnal (active during the day), since the scleral rings of the eyes were relatively small in comparison with its skull length.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus had a proportionally small brain with an encephalization quotient of 0.69, similar to sauropods.
facts.quote: The brain was proportionally small and compact, and its reptile encephalization quotient (brain-body ratio) was estimated at 0.69, which is low for theropods, and similar to sauropods.

facts.statement: In 2015, researchers found that Deinocheirus had the most pneumatized skeleton among ornithomimosaurs.
facts.quote: In 2015, Akinobu Watanabe and colleagues found that together with Archaeornithomimus and Gallimimus, Deinocheirus had the most pneumatised skeleton among ornithomimosaurs.

facts.statement: The function of pneumatization in Deinocheirus is debated, with hypotheses including bone mass reduction, high metabolism, locomotion balance, or thermoregulation.
facts.quote: It has been proposed that pneumatisation was used to reduce the mass of large bones (associated with gigantic size in the case of Deinocheirus), that it was related to high metabolism, balance during locomotion, or used for thermoregulation.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests the holotype specimen of Deinocheirus was a fully grown adult.
facts.quote: The structure of the periosteum and lack of growth arrest lines suggests that the holotype was a fully grown adult.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus had a weak bite force due to small muscle attachment sites relative to skull size.
facts.quote: The attachment sites for the muscles that open and close the jaws were very small in comparison to the size of the skull, which indicates Deinocheirus had a weak bite force.

facts.statement: Over 1,400 gastroliths ranging from 8 to 87mm in size were found in specimen MPC-D100/127.
facts.quote: More than 1,400 gastroliths (stomach stones, 8 to 87mm in size) were found among the ribs and gastralia of specimen MPC-D100/127.

facts.statement: The presence of fish vertebrae and scales among gastroliths suggests Deinocheirus was an omnivore.
facts.quote: In spite of these features, fish vertebrae and scales were also found among the gastroliths, which suggests that it was an omnivore.

facts.statement: A 2022 study found Deinocheirus showed unique stress and strain patterns in its jaws, indicating it was a specialized feeder.
facts.quote: A 2022 article by Waisum Ma and colleagues examined how feeding mechanics varied between different non-bird coelurosaurian groups through finite element analysis, revealing that they all underwent reduction of feeding-related stress in their jaws. They found that Deinocheirus showed different patterns of stress and strain distribution than other ornithomimisaurs, indicating it was a specialized feeder.

facts.statement: Researchers suspect Deinocheirus may have reverted to an omnivorous or carnivorous diet.
facts.quote: They suspected Deinocheirus may have reverted to omnivory/carnivory.

facts.statement: In 1970, Anatoly Konstantinovich Rozhdestvensky hypothesized that Deinocheirus was a specialized climbing dinosaur feeding on plants and animals in trees.
facts.quote: In 1970, the Russian paleontologist Anatoly Konstantinovich Rozhdestvensky compared the forelimbs of Deinocheirus to sloths, leading him to hypothesise that Deinocheirus was a specialised climbing dinosaur, that fed on plants and animals found in trees.

facts.statement: In 2017, it was suggested Deinocheirus's claws were adapted for pulling plants from water and reducing water resistance.
facts.quote: In 2017, it was suggested that the claws of Deinocheirus were adapted for pulling large quantities of herbaceous plants out of water, and to decrease the resistance of water.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Deinocheirus showed abnormal pits, grooves, and tubercles on finger phalanges, possibly from joint injuries.
facts.quote: Osmólska and Roniewicz reported palaeopathologies in the holotype specimen such as abnormal pits, grooves and tubercles on the first and second phalanx of the left second finger that may have been the result of injuries to the joint between the two bones.

facts.statement: In 2012, bite marks on the holotype's gastralia were identified as matching the teeth of Tarbosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2012, bite marks on two gastralia of the holotype specimen were reported. The size and shape of the bite marks match the teeth of Tarbosaurus, the largest known predator from the Nemegt Formation.

facts.statement: Researchers believe the bite marks on Deinocheirus represent feeding behavior where Tarbosaurus targeted internal organs.
facts.quote: The bite marks probably represent feeding behaviour instead of aggression between the species, and the fact that bite marks were not found elsewhere on the body indicates the predator focused on internal organs.

facts.statement: The river habitats where Deinocheirus lived supported a wide variety of other organisms including fish, turtles, and birds.
facts.quote: The habitats in and around the Nemegt rivers where Deinocheirus lived provided a home for a wide array of organisms.

facts.statement: The first remains of Deinocheirus, including large arm bones and shoulder girdles, were discovered in 1965 in the Nemegt Formation of Mongolia.
facts.quote: En 1965, un par de brazos grandes, fajas escapulares y algunos otros huesos de un nuevo dinosaurio se descubrieron por primera vez en la Formación Nemegt de Mongolia.

facts.statement: Two more complete specimens of Deinocheirus were described in 2014, providing new insights into the animal.
facts.quote: Se describieron dos especímenes más completos en 2014, que arrojan luz sobre muchos aspectos del animal.

facts.statement: Parts of the 2014 specimens had been looted from Mongolia years prior but were recovered and repatriated in 2014.
facts.quote: Partes de estos nuevos especímenes habían sido saqueados de Mongolia algunos años antes, pero fueron recuperados y repatriados en 2014.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus is classified in the family Deinocheiridae.
facts.quote: familia: Deinocheiridae

facts.statement: Deinocheirus belongs to the suborder Ornithomimosauria.
facts.quote: infraordo: Ornithomimosauria

facts.statement: Deinocheirus was the largest member of its clade, reaching 11 meters in length and weighing 6.36 tonnes.
facts.quote: Deinocheirus era un ornitomimosaurio inusual, el más grande del clado, con 11 metros de largo, y con 6,36 toneladas de peso.

facts.statement: Despite its large size, Deinocheirus had many hollow bones that reduced its weight.
facts.quote: Aunque era un animal voluminoso, tenía muchos huesos huecos que le ahorraban peso.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus possessed arms among the largest of any bipedal dinosaur, measuring 2.4 meters in length with large, blunt claws on three-fingered hands.
facts.quote: Los brazos estaban entre los más grandes de cualquier dinosaurio bípedo de 2,4 metros de largo, con grandes y romas garras en sus manos de tres dedos.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus had high neural spines on its vertebrae that formed a sail along its back.
facts.quote: Sus vértebras tenían altas espinas neurales que formaban una «vela» a lo largo de su espalda.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus's tail ended in pygostyle-like vertebrae, indicating the presence of a feather fan.
facts.quote: La cola termina en vértebras tipo pigostilo , que indican la presencia de un abanico de plumas.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus had a skull measuring 1.024 meters in length with a wide beak and deep lower jaw similar to hadrosaurs.
facts.quote: Su cráneo medía 1,024 metros de largo, con un pico ancho y una mandíbula inferior profunda, similar a los de los hadrosáuridos .

facts.statement: Deinocheirus's vertebrae had an interconnected ligament system that stiffened the spine to support the abdomen while transferring stress to the hips and hind limbs.
facts.quote: Las espinas vertebrales tenían un sistema de ligamentos interconectados, que volvía la columna vertebral más rígida y le permitió sostener el abdomen mientras transmitía el estrés a las caderas y las extremidades posteriores.

facts.statement: All of Deinocheirus's vertebrae were highly pneumatized with internal air sacs connected to the respiratory system, except for the atlas bone and the last tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: Todas las vértebras estaban altamente neumatizadas por los sacos de aire en su interior, a excepción del hueso atlas y las últimas vértebras de la cola, y por lo tanto estaban conectadas al sistema respiratorio.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus is believed to have been omnivorous, with skull shape indicating a plant diet, fish scales found near a specimen, and gastrolites present in the stomach region.
facts.quote: Se cree que Deinocheirus fue omnívoro, su forma de cráneo indica una dieta de plantas, se encontraron escamas de peces en asociación con un espécimen y gastrolitos también estaban presentes en la región del estómago del espécimen.

facts.statement: Bite marks on Deinocheirus bones have been attributed to the tyrannosaurid Tarbosaurus.
facts.quote: Las marcas de mordiscos en los huesos de Deinocheirus se han atribuido al tiranosáurido Tarbosaurus.

facts.statement: The large claws of Deinocheirus may have been used for digging and collecting plants.
facts.quote: Las garras grandes pueden haber sido utilizadas para cavar y recolectar plantas.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus's tail ended in at least two fused vertebrae described as similar to the pygostyles of oviraptorosaurian and therizinosaurian theropods.
facts.quote: La cola de Deinocheirus terminó en al menos dos vértebras fusionadas, que se describieron como similares al pigostilo de los terópodos oviraptorosaurianos y terizinosaurianos.

facts.statement: The classification of Deinocheirus was initially uncertain and placed in Carnosauria, but similarities to ornithomimosaurs were soon noted.
facts.quote: La clasificación de Deinocheirus era incierta, y se colocó inicialmente en el grupo de terópodos Carnosauria, pero las similitudes con ornitomimosaurianos pronto se notaron.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus mirificus lived between 71 and 69 million years ago during the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages of the Late Cretaceous in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: Deinocheirus mirificus (gr. «mano terrible inusual») es la única especie del género extinto Deinocheirus de dinosaurio deinoqueírido ornitomimosauriano, que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 71 a 69 millones de años, entre el Campaniense y el Maastrichtiense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: The only known skull of Deinocheirus measures 1.024 meters from the premaxilla to the back of the occipital condyle.
facts.quote: El único cráneo conocido, que pertenece al espécimen más grande, mide 1,024 metros desde el premaxilar hasta la parte posterior del cóndilo occipital.

facts.statement: The skull walls of Deinocheirus were quite thin, approximately 6 millimeters thick.
facts.quote: Las paredes óseas del cráneo eran bastante delgadas, aproximadamente 6 milímetros.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus had a rounded, flattened beak that would have been covered by keratin when alive.
facts.quote: Tenía un pico redondeado y aplanado, que habría sido cubierto por la queratina en vida.

facts.statement: The outer diameter of the sclerotic rings in Deinocheirus eyes was small, measuring 8.4 centimeters relative to skull size.
facts.quote: El diámetro exterior de los anillos escleróticos en los ojos era pequeño, 8,4 centímetros, en comparación con el tamaño del cráneo.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus had toothless jaws that turned downward, with a very large and deep lower jaw compared to its thin, low upper jaw.
facts.quote: Las mandíbulas eran desdentadas y giradas hacia abajo, y la mandíbula inferior era muy grande y profunda en comparación con la mandíbula superior delgada y baja.

facts.statement: The snout of Deinocheirus was spatulate and 25 centimeters wide, wider than the top of the skull.
facts.quote: El hocico era espatulado y de 25 centímetros de ancho, que es más ancho que el techo del cráneo.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus's blunt, short claws are similar to those of the therizinosaur Alxasaurus, suggesting its long arms and claws were used for digging and gathering plants.
facts.quote: Las garras romas y cortas de Deinocheirus son similares a las del tericinosáurido Alxasaurus, lo que indica que los brazos largos y las garras se usaron para cavar y recolectar plantas.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus likely used its long neural spines and possible tail fan for some type of visual display.
facts.quote: Las espinas neurales largas y la posible pantalla de cola pueden haberse utilizado para algún tipo de despliegue visual.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus was likely diurnal, active during the day, because its sclerotic rings were relatively small compared to skull length.
facts.quote: Deinocheirus era probablemente diurno, es decir, activo durante el día, ya que los anillos escleróticos de los ojos eran relativamente pequeños en comparación con la longitud de su cráneo.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus had a globular brain similar to birds and troodontid theropods, with relatively large olfactory tracts.
facts.quote: El cerebro era globular y de forma similar a la de las aves y los terópodos trodóntidos, el cerebro se expandió de forma similar a la mayoría de los terópodos y los tractos olfatorios fueron relativamente grandes.

facts.statement: A 2015 bone microstructure study suggested Deinocheirus likely had a high metabolic rate and grew rapidly before reaching sexual maturity.
facts.quote: Un estudio de microestructura ósea presentado en la 13.ª Reunión Anual de la Asociación Europea de Paleontólogos de Vertebrados en 2015 mostró que el Deinocheirus probablemente tenía una tasa metabólica alta y creció rápidamente antes de alcanzar la madurez sexual.

facts.statement: In 2015, Akinobu Watanabe and colleagues found that Deinocheirus had the most pneumatized skeleton among ornithomimosaurs, along with Archaeornithomimus and Gallimimus.
facts.quote: En 2015, Akinobu Watanabe y sus colegas encontraron que junto con Archaeornithomimus y Gallimimus, Deinocheirus tenía el esqueleto más neumatizado entre los ornitomimosaurianos.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus had a more specialized diet than other ornithomimosaurs, as shown by its distinctive skull shape.
facts.quote: La forma distintiva del cráneo muestra que Deinocheirus tenía una dieta más especializada que otros ornitomimosaurianos.

facts.statement: More than 1400 gastroliths, ranging from 8 to 87 millimeters in size, were found among the ribs and gastralia of specimen MPC-D100/127.
facts.quote: Se encontraron más de 1400 gastrolitos, piedras estomacales, de 8 a 87 milímetros de tamaño, entre las costillas y gastralia de la muestra MPC-D100/127.

facts.statement: Vertebrae and fish scales found among the gastroliths suggest Deinocheirus was an omnivore.
facts.quote: A pesar de estas características, también se encontraron vértebras y escamas de peces entre los gastrolitos, lo que sugiere que era un omnívoro.

facts.statement: In 2017, it was suggested that Deinocheirus's claws were adapted to extract large amounts of aquatic grasses and reduce water resistance.
facts.quote: En 2017, se sugirió que las garras de Deinocheirus se adaptaron para extraer grandes cantidades de plantas herbáceas del agua y para disminuir la resistencia del agua.

facts.statement: In 2012, bite marks on two gastralia of the holotype were reported, matching the size and shape of Tarbosaurus teeth, the largest known predator of the Nemegt Formation.
facts.quote: En 2012, se informaron marcas de mordiscos en dos gastralia del holotipo. El tamaño y la forma de las marcas de mordida coinciden con los dientes de Tarbosaurus, el depredador más grande conocido de la Formación Nemegt.

facts.statement: Before complete remains were known, Deinocheirus was imagined as a predator resembling an Allosaurus with giant arms, though this view has been debated.
facts.quote: Se propusieron varios comportamientos de alimentación antes de que se conocieran los restos más completos de Deinocheirus, y desde el principio se lo imaginó como un depredador, un animal parecido a un Allosaurus con brazos gigantes.

facts.statement: In 1970, Anatoly Konstantinovich Rozhdestvensky hypothesized that Deinocheirus was a specialized climbing dinosaur feeding on plants and animals in trees, based on comparing its forelimbs to sloths.
facts.quote: En 1970, el paleontólogo ruso Anatoly Konstantinovich Rozhdestvensky comparó las extremidades anteriores de Deinocheirus con los perezosos, lo que lo llevó a la hipótesis de que Deinocheirus era un dinosaurio especializado en escalar, que se alimentaba de plantas y animales que se encuentran en los árboles.

facts.statement: In 1988, Gregory S. Paul suggested Deinocheirus's claws were too blunt for predation but would have served as good defensive weapons.
facts.quote: En 1988, Gregory S. Paul en cambio sugirió que las garras eran demasiado contundentes con fines depredadores, pero que habrían sido buenas armas defensivas.

facts.statement: A cladogram based on research by Barsbold et al. in 2014 was produced to classify Deinocheirus.
